title: Traffic smoothing: region warm-standby, weighted switchover and KV reconciliation runbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: provide an operational runbook for graceful cross-region traffic smoothing that (1) warms standby capacity, (2) performs tenant-weighted canary shifts, and (3) reconciles KV cache divergence for Hosted and Dedicated customers. This document codifies detection thresholds, stepwise manual actions, and automated playbox hooks to reduce user-facing errors during region-level capacity degradation.
impact_summary: High customer impact if not executed: potential token-level errors, elevated latency for latency-sensitive tenants, and possible KV cache divergence causing stale streaming completions. Target SLO: avoid >5% request error uplift and keep median p50 generation latency degradation <25% during incident handling for top-tier tenants.
detection: Signals to trigger runbook: 1) region control-plane health alert (>=3 control-plane instances failing in 2m), 2) sustained P90 request latency increase >2x baseline for 5+ minutes, 3) per-tenant error-rate spike >=1% absolute and >3x baseline, 4) autoscaler failure or GPU drain events reported from provider. Correlate with: infra-monitoring, console per-route latency charts, and dedicated cluster dashboard.
prechecks: Before executing: 1) confirm exact impacted region and datacenter IDs, 2) identify affected clusters and whether customers are on Hosted vs Dedicated, 3) gather top-10 affected tenants by qps and SLA tier, 4) check standby region warm capacity (GPUs and routing) and verify KV store replication status, 5) ensure SRE/PM/SE pager rotation is notified.
mitigation_steps: 1) Open incident channel and label priority. 2) If Hosted: enable smart-routing rule to redirect only non-priority traffic to warm standby (apply weighted rule 90/10 start). 3) If Dedicated: coordinate with customer account manager and toggle customer-specific ingress to standby (do not change global routing). 4) Warm standby: provision transient instances or enable reserved pool; pre-load model weights for top-3 affected models. 5) KV reconciliation: run snapshot compare for KV prefixes used by sticky routing and streaming contexts; if mismatch >0.1% for active prefixes, trigger KV re-sync job for those prefixes. 6) Canary: shift 5% of prioritized tenants for 2 minutes, validate success metrics (error rate <0.5% and latency <150% baseline), then double every 2 minutes to 10%, 20%, 40% while monitoring. 7) Traffic smoothing: use exponential-weight smoothing (0.2 step) in routing to avoid request bursts. 8) If any validation fails at canary stage, immediately rollback to previous weights and investigate logs and tail traces.
execution_notes: - Use console feature 'traffic-weights' for hosted; CLI flow for dedicated: 'rictl route update --weights'. - For Dedicated customers, inform SE to temporarily change tenant routing only after explicit customer approval if required by contract. - Prioritize GPU-backed warm caches for models with long load times (GPT-style). - Avoid mass eviction of KV caches; prefer prefix sync unless cache is irrecoverably corrupted.
rollback_steps: 1) Revert traffic weights to last known-good using console or rictl. 2) If KV resync introduced divergence, restore KV from pre-run snapshot and abort in-flight resync. 3) If warm-standby resources cause instability, drain traffic back and deprovision transient nodes after stabilization. 4) Post-rollback: run postmortem validation queries for affected tenants and open follow-up bug tickets.
validation_checks: During and after shift validate: 1) per-tenant error rate and p95 latency via console dashboards, 2) sample LLM outputs for semantic correctness for a curated prompt set (top routes), 3) trace sampling for root-cause analysis, 4) KV prefix checksum parity for top prefixes.
automation_hooks: - Incident playbook should trigger automated partial-weight shift if latency exceeds threshold for 10m with optional manual confirmation. - Built-in circuit-breaker to stop automated increases if error-rate crosses 0.8% for any shifted tenant. - Use canary-tokens service to auto-validate model responses for correctness during shift.
testing_plan: 1) Quarterly simulated degrade drill: inject artificial latency into primary region at 9am PT on dry-run window. 2) Run end-to-end rehearsal with staging tenants mapped to Dedicated clusters. 3) Validate KV resync tool on low-risk prefixes and capture durations. 4) Run blast radius analysis to confirm escalation path and communication templates.
post_incident_followup: Mandatory items after incident: 1) 72h timeline draft and owner list, 2) PR for any hotfix merged with link to CI run, 3) update runbook with lessons and parameter tweaks, 4) customer-facing incident summary for affected tenants (review by legal/communications).
roles_and_owners: SREs: lead execution (Marcus Kim), Infra on-call: cluster provisioning, Platform: routing changes, SE/AM: customer comms for Dedicated tenants, PM: triage priority and SLA decisions.
